Frantz Fanon was a psychiatrist and writer born in Fort-de-France, Martinique, in 1925, whose books became central texts of anti-colonial thought. He was taught at school by Aime Cesaire.

He fought for Free France in World War II and studied in Lyon. His first book, Black Skin, White Masks (1952), examined the psychology of racism. Working at a hospital in Algeria, he joined the independence side in the Algerian War.

The Wretched of the Earth (1961), written as he was dying of leukaemia, argued that colonised peoples must free themselves, by violence if needed. It inspired movements from Africa to the Black Panthers in America. He died at 36 and was buried in Algeria. He remains a major figure in postcolonial studies.
